content.user_title: Model STRIDE Threats for System Designs
content.value_statement: Security reviews often miss threats when teams lack a repeatable method. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through STRIDE analysis, risk ranking, and mitigation planning.
actual_capabilities: Maps system components to the six STRIDE threat categories.
Provides threat model document templates with assets, boundaries, risks, and mitigations.
Offers questionnaires for reviewing components against common security concerns.
Analyzes data flow diagrams for trust boundary crossings and unencrypted flows.
Suggests common mitigations for spoofing, tampering, repudiation, disclosure, denial, and privilege risks.
Helps prioritize threats with impact, likelihood, and risk score examples.
limitations: It does not perform automated code scanning or penetration testing.
It depends on accurate architecture, asset, and data flow inputs from the user.
Example code is instructional and may need adaptation before production use.
It cannot replace expert review for regulated or high-risk systems.

use_cases.title: Review a New Service Design
use_cases.description: Identify STRIDE threats, trust boundaries, and priority mitigations before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Prepare Audit Evidence
use_cases.description: Create structured threat documentation that links assets, risks, and recommended controls.

use_cases.title: Teach Threat Modeling Workshops
use_cases.description: Use templates and questionnaires to help engineers practice systematic threat identification.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic STRIDE Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for a small service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a web service with users, an API, and a database. List threats by STRIDE category and suggest mitigations.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Trust Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze these components and data flows. Identify trust boundary crossings, unencrypted flows, and related STRIDE threats.

prompt_templates.title: Create Threat Model Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a threat model document for this architecture. Include assets, boundaries, threat tables, risk ratings, and recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Complex Architecture Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare threats across these services. Rank risks by impact and likelihood, then propose phased mitigations and verification steps.

output_examples.input: A public web app sends payment requests to an internal billing API and stores customer data in a database.
output_examples.output: The review highlights spoofing risks at login, tampering risks in payment requests, disclosure risks for customer data, and rate limiting for availability.

output_examples.input: A team provides a data flow diagram with external users, an API gateway, workers, queues, and storage.
output: Trust boundary crossings are identified between external users and the gateway.
Unencrypted queue traffic is marked as an information disclosure risk.
Worker permissions are reviewed for elevation of privilege exposure.

output_examples.input: An auditor asks for evidence that a new service was threat modeled before release.
output_examples.output: The generated document summarizes assets, STRIDE findings, prioritized risks, owners, mitigations, and follow-up verification tasks.

best_practices: Provide architecture diagrams, assets, trust boundaries, and data classifications before asking for analysis.
Review every STRIDE category for each important component or interaction.
Convert high-priority threats into owned mitigation tasks with verification steps.
anti_patterns: Skipping categories because a threat seems unlikely without documenting the reason.
Using generic mitigations without linking them to specific assets or flows.
Treating the generated model as final without stakeholder validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help analyze?
faq.answer: It helps analyze systems, components, data flows, trust boundaries, and interactions with the STRIDE threat modeling method.

faq.question: Does it run security tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured analysis guidance, templates, and example logic for threat modeling.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Architecture diagrams, component lists, data classifications, authentication flows, and known trust boundaries produce better results.

faq.question: Can it create audit-ready documentation?
faq.answer: It can draft structured documentation, but teams should validate accuracy, ownership, and final risk decisions.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill is intended for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it replace a security architect?
faq.answer: No. It supports systematic review, but expert judgment is still needed for complex or regulated systems.
